systems.title: Systems I Build
systems.intro: Three architectures from production work, drawn as living diagrams. Hover a node to see what it does and what it talks to; the moving dots are the data. No client data is shown, only how the systems are put together.
systems.hint: Hover or focus a node to see its role.
systems.nda: Client names, endpoints and numbers are intentionally left out; the shapes are real.

gaming.title: Real-time game platform
gaming.summary: Canvas game clients, a WebSocket game server that owns the truth, provably fair RNG and an idempotent wallet behind one gateway.

player.title: Player
player.desc: Any browser or in-app webview; treated as untrusted input.

client.title: Canvas client
client.desc: Shared HTML5 Canvas engine: rendering, animation, assets, sound and UI state as reusable modules, so a new game is mostly configuration.

gateway.title: API gateway
gateway.desc: Fastify edge: auth (JWT / OAuth 2.0 / 2FA), rate limits, WebSocket upgrade and routing to game servers over gRPC.

server.title: Game server
server.desc: Node.js + WebSocket, server-authoritative: the client only sends intents, the server decides every outcome and broadcasts state.

rng.title: Provably fair RNG
rng.desc: HMAC-SHA256 over server seed, client seed and nonce; the seed hash is committed before the bet and revealed afterwards.

wallet.title: Wallet settlement
wallet.desc: Debit and credit with idempotency keys, so a retried request can never double-charge or double-pay.

redis.title: Redis
redis.desc: Round state, session mapping and pub/sub so any server instance can serve a reconnecting player.

events.title: Event bus
events.desc: Kafka / RabbitMQ topics for bets, results and settlements consumed by downstream services.

analytics.title: Analytics
analytics.desc: ClickHouse pipeline for RTP monitoring, funnels and operator reporting.

authoritative.title: Server-authoritative state
authoritative.desc: The client never decides an outcome. Intents go up, results and full state come down.

idempotent.title: Idempotent settlement
idempotent.desc: Every wallet write carries a key; retries after a timeout are safe by construction.

resume.title: Reconnect-and-resume
resume.desc: Sequence numbers on every message; a dropped player resumes from the last acknowledged round.

fair.title: Provably fair by default
fair.desc: Seed commitment before play, reveal after, so players can verify any round themselves.

broadcast.title: Live broadcast graphics
broadcast.summary: A sports data feed becomes on-air match graphics for six sports, with fan-out across instances and catch-up in about a second.

feed.title: Data feed
feed.desc: Upstream provider WebSocket with match status snapshots; reconnects with backoff when it drops.

ingest.title: Ingest
ingest.desc: Normalises status codes and coordinates, keeps the latest snapshot per match and publishes changes.

pubsub.title: Redis pub/sub
pubsub.desc: Fan-out channel so every socket instance receives every match update.

socketA.title: Socket server A
socketA.desc: socket.io instance with one room per match; clients join by match id.

socketB.title: Socket server B
socketB.desc: Second instance behind the same nginx upstream; horizontal scale without sticky state.

admin.title: Admin panel
admin.desc: Operator UI for enabling matches, themes and sponsor slots.

tv.title: TV overlay
tv.desc: Full-screen browser scene rendered on the broadcast machine.

iframe.title: Embedded tracker
iframe.desc: Operator websites embed the same scene as an iframe with their own theme.

cache.title: Snapshot cache
cache.desc: Latest state per match with a TTL, served over REST when a client first connects.

snapshot.title: Snapshot first, then stream
snapshot.desc: A new or reconnecting client loads the cached snapshot, then attaches to the stream. Nothing is missed.

fanout.title: Pub/sub fan-out
fanout.desc: Instances are stateless; Redis carries every update so any of them can serve any client.

rooms.title: One room per match
rooms.desc: Clients receive only the match they watch, which keeps bandwidth and rendering cost flat.

embed.title: Themeable embed
embed.desc: The same React scene runs on TV and inside operator sites, themed from config.

multibrand.title: Config-driven multi-brand frontend
multibrand.summary: One React + TypeScript codebase shipping several brands: tokens, components and permissions all come from configuration.

config.title: Brand config
config.desc: Per-brand JSON: colours, fonts, feature flags, enabled modules and locale list.

tokens.title: Design tokens
tokens.desc: CSS variables generated from config; Tailwind reads them, so every component re-skins without code changes.

components.title: Component library
components.desc: Shared UI kit with framer-motion transitions; brands compose pages from the same pieces.

rbac.title: Roles & flags
rbac.desc: Route-level role checks and feature flags decide what each user and brand can see.

brandA.title: Brand A
brandA.desc: Casino-first brand: slots, live casino, tournaments.

brandB.title: Brand B
brandB.desc: Sportsbook-first brand with the same component kit and a different token set.

brandC.title: Brand C
brandC.desc: White-label demo brand switched on by config alone.

cms.title: Strapi CMS
cms.desc: Centralised content: pages, promotions and translations pulled over REST.

ci.title: CI/CD
ci.desc: GitHub Actions builds each brand, ships Docker images behind nginx and PM2.

configDriven.title: Config over code
configDriven.desc: Adding a brand means adding a JSON file, not a fork.

rbac.title: Role-based access at the route
rbac.desc: Permissions are enforced where navigation happens, not sprinkled through components.

caching.title: Server state with TanStack Query
caching.desc: Caching, retries and background refresh handled centrally; Redux Toolkit keeps only UI and session state.

i18n.title: i18n from day one
i18n.desc: i18next namespaces per module; new languages are content, not code.
